A total of 14 teams competed in the tournament, with [[Alianza Lima]] as the defending champion. [[Alianza Lima]] won its twenty-first Primera División title after beating [[Sporting Cristal]] in the final playoff.[https://historialblanquiazul.com/temporada-2004/ Alianza Lima temporada 2004][https://www.infobae.com/2004/12/30/159853-alianza-lima-gano-el-titulo-la-liga-peruana-2004/ Alianza Lima ganó el título de la Liga peruana de 2004][https://elcomercio.pe/deporte-total/futbol-peruano/alianza-lima-con-butron-waldir-jayo-y-costas-como-protagonistas-revive-el-titulo-del-2004-fotos-noticia/ Alianza Lima: con Butrón, Waldir, Jayo y Costas como protagonistas, revive el título del 2004] ==Changes from 2003== ===Structural changes=== The number of teams for the 2004 season grew from 12 to 14. The relegation system was re-introduced but the system was determined by a points per match average. The qualification for the Copa Sudamericana was determined by the aggregate table instead of the Torneo Apertura playoffs. Due to a structure change in the Copa Libertadores, only two teams will qualify directly to the group stage (the half-year champions) and the best-placed non-champion will have to play in the first stage. ===Promotion and relegation=== No teams were relegated from the 2003 season and thus the number of teams grew from 12 to 14. [[Segunda División Peruana 2003|Segunda División]] champion [[Sport Coopsol]] and Copa Perú 2003 champion [[C.D. Universidad César Vallejo|Universidad César Vallejo]] were promoted. [[Club Deportivo Universidad de San Martín de Porres|Universidad San Martín]] bought the promotional place of the [[2003 Segunda División Peruana|2003 Segunda División]] winners, [[Sport Coopsol]]. ===Team changes=== {| class="wikitable" |- !
